value.body: An automotive service engineer works in after-sales: diagnosing faults, guiding workshop technicians, handling warranty cases and sending field-failure reports back to the maker. Employers include vehicle makers' service divisions, authorised dealerships and fleet operators. The day is split between the workshop floor, customers and reporting.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Tech or diploma in Automobile or Mechanical Engineering

items.label: Common tools
items.value: On-board diagnostics (OBD) scan tools, dealer management software

items.label: Domestic vehicle sales
items.note: Wholesales, all categories; up ~10% on FY 2024-25

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers join dealerships or a vehicle maker's service team as trainees, often starting in the workshop. A driving licence is usually expected, and some roles need travel across a region.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Basics of electric and hybrid vehicles

value.title: At a glance
items: Customer-facing work, including weekends at some dealerships.
Workshop experience can count toward state Motor Vehicle Inspector eligibility in some states.
Next roles: service manager, regional service lead, warranty or quality analyst.

competition.note: B.Tech / B.E. (all branches) graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
competition.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education
